title: Travel cards in the UAE: 6 options compared
summary: In this guide, we’ll compare popular travel cards in the UAE, break down their fees and features, and help you find the right option for you.
body_markdown:
If you’ve traveled outside of the UAE before, you’ve probably had this moment: you check your bank account after getting home and wonder why your trip cost more than you expected.


It often isn't the flights or hotels that catch you out. It's the small things. Paying for coffee, grabbing an Uber, shopping in a local market. Every time you swipe your everyday card, you might be adding more foreign transaction fees or currency conversion charges to your bill.


The good news is that there are plenty of travel cards designed to make spending overseas easier and more cost-effective nowadays. The challenge is knowing which one to choose.


That's where this guide comes in. We'll compare six of some popular travel cards available to UAE residents, break down their fees and features, and help you find the right option for the way you travel.

These products are not identical: the comparison includes virtual, prepaid and credit cards with different eligibility requirements, fees and benefits. The right option will depend on the customer’s spending habits and travel needs.


## How to choose the right card for spending abroad from the UAE


While there’s no ‘best’ card for spending abroad, finding the right one for you comes down to how you use it.


For example, before deciding on a card, ask:


- What do the conversion fees look like?


Using a regular UAE card abroad could sometimes cost you 2% – 3% per transaction in currency conversion fees. Travel cards, on the other hand, are designed to keep those costs lower – sometimes as low as 0%. It is also important to review subscription, ATM, card issuance and other applicable charges, as these may affect the overall cost.


- Are you a frequent flyer?


If you want to earn airline miles or get airport lounge access, look for a card that offers travel rewards and benefits that match the way you fly. Some providers partner with specific airlines, so it may be worth choosing a card linked to the airline you use most often.


- Do you often travel in the GCC area?


Depending on the provider, certain cards may offer more competitive fees when spending in neighboring GCC countries.


- Are you interested in brand discounts?


Some premium cards include perks like VPN access, free hotel stays, discounts for booking platforms, or complimentary travel insurance. These cards might also offer


[deals for UAE-based brands](https://ziina.com/personal/plans/violet) , which is great for when you aren’t traveling.


- What level of security is important to you?


Look for cards with easy app controls, instant freeze/unfreeze buttons, and fast customer support to protect against fraud. Virtual cards might also come with Face ID or virtual PIN numbers, which can add another layer of protection.


As a general rule, the right card is usually one that offers low currency conversion fees up to a limit that suits you, provides benefits that are important to you, and actually matches how often you travel.


Note: Make sure to check the minimum salary and eligibility requirements for each card, since that can quickly narrow down your options in the UAE.


Let’s get into our five options!


## Ziina: Easily spend overseas with a virtual card


We’ll start by introducing ourselves: Ziina is a UAE peer-to-peer payment app that helps you travel overseas and keep costs low each time you swipe your card.


Using Ziina’s virtual card, you can spend directly from your Ziina Wallet anywhere that Visa is accepted. Add the card to e-wallets like Apple Pay or Google Pay, and check your balance anytime within the Ziina app (which updates quickly with every transaction).


A Ziina Card is free to create and helps you save on international spending with 0% currency conversion fees up to your


[account limit](https://ziina.com/faq) . This depends on what type of Ziina account you have:


- Ziina Lite:


Spend 3,000 AED per month without any currency conversion fees, and only pay a 0.5% fee for amounts over this limit.


- Ziina Violet:


Spend 20,000 AED per month without any currency conversion fees, also with a 0.5% fee for any amount spent over the limit. You can also enjoy benefits from brands you love with over 850 AED in value each month.


For example, if you're using Ziina Lite and spend the equivalent of 4,000 AED in foreign currencies in one month, you'll only pay the 0.5% currency conversion fee on the AED 1,000 above your allowance. That's a fee of AED 5.


Other than that, the Ziina Card has zero fees for local AED transactions in the UAE. You don’t need to worry about sign-up fees or hidden fees, either.

### Get advanced security features like card freezing, Face ID, and instant card replacement


As a virtual-only card, Ziina enables you to control all your details from the app, which is protected by multi-factor authentication and your phone's built-in biometric security (like Face ID or your fingerprint scanner). All card details are encrypted and stored using PCI-DSS-compliant security standards.


You can freeze your Ziina Card through the app if you believe your card has been subject to fraud. There’s no need to call or wait for customer support to do this: instead, you can just head to the card management section of the app and click the ‘Freeze’ button.

Here are some other travel cards in the UAE to consider…


## Al Ansari Exchange Platinum TravelCard


The prepaid Al Ansari Exchange Platinum TravelCard


1 is a reloadable prepaid card that allows you to manage up to 37 currencies at once. You can use the card to pay for goods, services, and bills, or to withdraw money from ATMs across the world (where Visa is accepted).


Key rewards and perks


- Add your card to Apple Pay, Samsung Wallet or Google Wallet


- Chip and PIN protected


- Get up to 5 supplementary cards for your family


- Reload and manage your money on the Al Ansari Exchange App


- Lock in rates before travel and avoid currency fluctuations


Eligibility requirements:


To apply for the Al Ansari Exchange Visa Platinum TravelCard, you need to be a UAE resident with a valid Emirates ID that’s over the age of 18.


1b To apply for a TravelCard, visit any of the Al Ansari Exchange branches across the UAE.


Annual cost:


Costs vary depending on which card services and features you use. For example, there’s a digital issuance fee of 50 AED, a card reload/unload fee of 5 AED, and it costs 30 AED for every supplementary card you create.


1a


Might be the right fit for:


Users looking for multi-currency spending options.


## ADCB Traveller Credit Card


The ADCB Traveller Credit Card


2 is a travel-focused rewards credit card issued by the Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank. Frequent flyers can earn up to AED 1,500 cashback per month rates on flights and hotels with waived foreign currency fees.


To access these cashback rewards, you’ll have to meet a minimum retail spend of AED 5,000 or more using your card in a calendar month. It’s worth noting that overseas retail purchases other than airline and hotel bookings seemingly won’t be eligible for cashback rewards.


Key rewards and perks:


- 0 currency conversion fees


- 10% cashback on airline tickets and hotel stays


- 14 complimentary visits to airport lounges worldwide for you and your supplementary cardholders, plus 1 free guest per visit


- 4 complimentary airport rides per year, saving up to AED 85 on each ride


- Complimentary travel insurance that includes medical and inconvenience cover, plus a car rental collision and loss damage waiver


Eligibility requirements:


- To apply for an ADCB Traveller Credit Card, you should be at least 18 years old and either:


- Have a minimum salary of AED 20,000


- Or be eligible for a credit limit of at least AED 30,000


You’ll also need a minimum balance of AED 5000 to open an ADCB account, which lets you then apply for the ADCB Traveller Credit Card


2 .


Annual cost:


There’s an annual membership fee of 1,575 AED per year to maintain this card.


2a


Might be the right fit for:


High spenders looking for cashback rewards on airline and hotel bookings.


## Emirates NBD Skywards Infinite Credit Card


The Emirates Skyward Visa Infinite Card


3 is a premium co-branded credit card designed for frequent flyers. It’s designed for frequent flyers to earn loyalty rewards, fast-track elite status, and access luxury travel perks.


Please note that overseas transactions made with your Emirates Skywards Card are subject to a 1.99% currency conversion fee (subject to terms and conditions and the latest pricing information).


3a


Key rewards and perks:


- As a welcome offer, you can get up to 100,000 bonus Skywards Miles and complimentary Rotana Rewards membership for one year


- Complimentary Emirates Skywards Silver membership upgrade, with access to the Business Class Lounge


- Complimentary access to over 1,000 airport lounges worldwide via the Visa Airport Companion app


Eligibility requirements:


To apply for this card, you’ll need to be a UAE resident, hold a valid Emirates ID, and be over the age of 18. You’ll also need to earn a minimum of 30,000 AED per month, and pay a one-time joining fee of 3,148.95 AED.


3a


Annual cost:


It costs 1,575 AED to maintain this card each year.


3a


Might be the right fit for:


Frequent flyers and high-income earners in the UAE who want premium travel perks (such as airport lounge access).


Note:


Emirates NBD also offers another travel card, the Skywards Signature Credit Card


3b , which offers lower annual fees and lower annual income requirements than the Skyward Visa Infinite card.


## FAB Travel Credit Card


The FAB Travel Credit Card


4 is a premium travel rewards credit card issued by First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) in the United Arab Emirates that waives international transaction fees and bank charges when you use your card abroad.


Key rewards and perks:


- 12% cashback in FAB Rewards on flight and hotel bookings, up to a maximum of 1,800 AED per month, subject to meeting a minimum monthly spend of 5,000 AED


- 14 complimentary visits per year to airport lounges worldwide for you and your supplementary cardholders


- Get 4 airport transfers per year to and from UAE airports


- Get up to 35% off car rentals with Avis


- A free return flight from over 15 regional & global destinations, subject to payment of the annual membership fee and meeting the minimum 300,000 AED spend requirements during the previous year)


Eligibility requirements:


To open a FAB Travel Credit Card, you’ll need to be a UAE resident, be over 18 years old, hold a valid Emirates ID, and meet the minimum salary requirement of 20,000 AED per month.


Annual cost:


It costs 1,500 AED per year to maintain this credit card, though you’ll also pay 241.50 AED for any late payments you make.


4a


Might be the right fit for:


Frequent flyers looking for flight and travel insurance benefits.
